policy.applicableSecurityMd: None; empty results for each of the six source files.
policy.instructions: Read Codex Security finding-discovery SKILL.md and security-guidance.md. The parent owns candidate recording and scan assembly.

conclusion: No technically plausible new security candidate identified in the complete diff of the assigned six files. This is a bounded discovery result, not a whole-repository security attestation. Two non-vulnerability limitations are preserved below instead of being dropped.

coverage.attackerInput: Named metadata file bytes supplied in authenticated source archive intake, including comments, formatter JSON, npmrc entries and example environment names/values.
reviewedControls: 16 KiB length bound and fatal UTF-8 decoding before grammar parsing
Control character/known-secret pattern check before ignoring comments
Finite npmrc and formatter keys/value types
Example env VITE_ name restrictions, duplicate detection, public-placeholder grammar and credential/query/fragment-free URL constraints
No evaluator, child process, network operation or metadata application sink
negativeResults: The accepted .npmrc grammar contains only strict-peer-dependencies and shell-emulator boolean data. The preview compiler never runs npm or reads .npmrc as execution configuration.
Examples permit only fixed scalar placeholders or bounded loopback/reserved-domain URLs and do not populate runtime.environment. Unknown variables are refused by runtime analysis.

Secret-pattern detection is deliberately finite and can neither classify every credential nor make all source secret-free. Accepted comments/metadata are private project bytes; no newly reachable cross-tenant or external disclosure sink was established.
coverage.validationPerformed: Source inspection only; no tests or payload execution.

coverage.attackerInput: ZIP member paths, ZIP attributes, compressed/expanded data, metadata basenames.
reviewedControls: safeArchivePath remains the shared path guard; bounded .env.example[-suffix] is the only env-name expansion
Existing absolute/traversal/backslash/colon/NFC/reserved-name/depth/member-name guard preserved
ZIP member mode/link/encryption/case-conflict/size/ratio/CRC/UTF-8 checks preserved
All member validation finishes before private filesystem writes
Metadata validation now occurs before files.set and archive admission
negativeResults: The name expansion does not relax parent traversal, absolute path, symlink/hardlink or cross-project destination handling. Hosted caller allocates a fresh temporary tree, and export/shared source validation continue to use safeArchivePath.

The existing extension allowlist admits some dot-prefixed files independently of isInertMetadata; that behavior predates this diff. The README/test title is broader than actual coverage, but this is not a newly introduced arbitrary-file admission path.
Intake and hosted source copying preserve accepted metadata as bytes; source edits/history/export do not turn metadata into editor-host configuration.
coverage.baseComparison: The general file-extension allowlist and original .env.example admission are already present in base projectRegistry.ts:45-87. Only the finite name/grammar expansion is new.

coverage.attackerInput: Uploaded package manifest/lock, local Vite config AST, aliases, inert server/preview settings and CSS source.
reviewedControls: Fixed repository profile IDs and full declared-set candidate preference
Versions/lock root declarations/integrity and installed version checks retained
New client closure derives from trusted profileLock; visited set bounds trusted graph traversal
Path.resolve is interpreted as a finite AST form and checked through confinedFile
Unknown statements/imports/plugins/computed object fields and dynamic expressions rejected
Null-prototype interpreted objects and aliases reject duplicate keys
Server open/port preferences validated as boolean/bounded integer and preserved only
Exception-to-issue handling keeps unsupported input out of compiler admission
negativeResults: Uploaded lock bytes never cause dependency installation; they are compared to a repository-owned profile. An altered lock record can fail admission but cannot select arbitrary package code.
Static path.resolve and no-argument arrow factories do not invoke imported functions. Paths pass safeArchivePath plus root/realpath confinement; aliases cannot select operator files.

New recursive AST cases do not add an evaluator; malformed or unsupported syntax/errors become runtime issues. Existing parser work runs editor-side; no new independently supported fatal-process or unbounded-resource exploit was established from these finite additions.

Peer dependencies are omitted by both the new and retained traversals; a new use-immer peer is a concrete exact-lock compatibility gap. It does not make uploaded package bytes executable because resolution still uses the installed trusted profile.

coverage.attackerInput: CSS @theme custom-property values and ordinary CSS declarations.
reviewedControls: Added color-function recognizer is anchored and accepts only a fixed function name/finite channel count/numeric grammar
No var/url/calc/exponent/general function invocation accepted by literalColor
Root-only @theme, custom-property naming, no !important/nested nodes, known directive denials retained
PostCSS parses structure before pinned Tailwind consumes the bounded data subset
negativeResults: The new accepted literal color strings remain compiler data and contain no route to Node config/plugin execution.
Rejected function syntax or declaration separators cannot bypass the parsed node-level @theme checks through this helper.

No exponential or attacker-controlled recursive execution sink was identified in the added fixed-channel regexes. Existing input size bounds and compiler/parse behavior remain separate resource controls.

coverage.attackerInput: Source import strings, CSS resource URLs/data URLs, declarations requiring newly admitted browser closure packages.
reviewedControls: External URL exception is limited to HTTP transport and CSS url/import-token resolution
HTTP(S) URL userinfo rejected; external:true preserves a reference without a compiler fetch
Data exception only for listed image/font MIME types and url-token, not arbitrary remote JavaScript imports
Application imports must match runtime.clientDependencies and dependency resolution must realpath into profile node_modules
Project-relative/alias/public paths retain permitted-root confinement
Trusted esbuild/Tailwind processing remains browser-targeted and writes no executable artifact to host disk
negativeResults: CSS preservation does not create editor-side SSRF: no fetch API exists in the added branch. The browser can attempt external requests, but the unchanged worker intentionally passes them to the private Linux network namespace; default external=deny is retained.

The closure admission expansion does not install or evaluate uploaded dependencies/config. Packages resolved through the profile are read as source; uploaded Node modules are not executed in the compiler.

Editor-side compilation precedes Linux runner allocation. The existing compiler gate reserves a transport entry after async authorization, while source/checkpoint validation uses the same confined compiler. New URL/profile behavior does not alter these admission controls.

The pre-existing non-strict local Blob branch is a separate execution mode. This added remote-CSS exception requires transport=http, and strict HostedEditor uses controlled raster with no Blob fallback.
supportingPathChecks: Fast Refresh Babel invocation explicitly disables babelrc/configFile and emits generated browser code rather than executing imported source in Node (src/webcanbe-engine/runtime/fastRefreshCompiler.ts:32-86).

coverage.attackerInput: Repository-authored synthetic metadata/config/CSS/lock examples; tests are developer-controlled, not product request handlers.
reviewedControls: Temporary fixture copies and per-test cleanup
Metadata byte-preservation/rejection cases
Static aliases/factory/proxy rejection cases
Trusted profile selection and unresolved import rejection
Numeric CSS-function acceptance/rejection cases
One transitive tippy.js integrity-tampering assertion
Remote-CSS data preservation vs remote-JS refusal
Exact pointer-frame tuple comparisons
negativeResults: No new product endpoint, credential provisioning, uploaded config evaluation or shell execution exists in this test file.
The malicious-looking shell string in a test is a literal archive member value passed to validation, not executed.
The arbitrary-dotfiles test exercises .credentials only, so its title is not evidence of blanket dotfile rejection. The transitive-lock test exercises tippy.js dependencies, not peer dependencies.
The tests were inspected, not run, and do not prove OS sandbox/egress enforcement or all integration properties.

supplementalCorrections.classification: Exact-lock compatibility correction; no security candidate emitted
supplementalCorrections.control: runtimeCompatibility.ts traverses dependencies only; newly allowed use-immer declares immer as a peer.
supplementalCorrections.prerequisite: An imported manifest declares react/react-dom/vite and use-immer but not direct immer; its uploaded lock records the expected direct roots and a missing/different immer peer record.
supplementalCorrections.currentEffect: The inspected traversal need not compare that peer's uploaded version/integrity, while the compiler still resolves trusted installed immer. This violates a complete reachable-lock equivalence claim without selecting attacker package bytes.
supplementalCorrections.recommendation: Visit the union of dependencies and peerDependencies through the existing path-aware resolver. Skip optional peers absent from the trusted graph; verify optional peers present in it; refuse missing required peers. Keep nested resolution rather than extending the old top-level-only DFS.
supplementalCorrections.regression: Use the React19/Vite7 common profile with direct use-immer but no direct immer: matching lock passes, changing only node_modules/immer integrity/version fails. For React18/Vite6 common with direct zustand, its optional immer/use-sync-external-store peers absent from the trusted graph remain allowed, while an altered present @types/react peer record fails.
supplementalCorrections.validationStatus: Source-backed recommendation only. Parent intends implementation/testing outside this immutable result.

supplementalCorrections.classification: Documentation/test-scope correction; existing behavior, no security candidate emitted
supplementalCorrections.claim: README says arbitrary dotfiles and credentials remain refused; test title also refers to arbitrary dotfiles.
supplementalCorrections.actualControl: Finite named metadata validation plus a general file-extension allowlist. Non-example env names are refused, but other dot-prefixed extension-matching source filenames remain possible. Known credential patterns are not a universal classifier.
supplementalCorrections.impactPrerequisiteMissing: No newly gained access to another actor's secrets, source, environment or operator authority was identified; own uploaded bytes remain source data.

retainedLimits: Installed runtime profile contents and privileged operator preparation are trusted configuration inputs; runtime checks are not a complete installed-file hash audit.

Linux cgroups constrain imported browser/config execution in separately authorized jobs, not the Mac/editor compiler. Existing process-local compiler admission and parser bounds should not be represented as fleet-wide compiler isolation.
Ordinary source/history/export authorization, mTLS fencing and Linux sandbox implementations were used as supporting controls rather than reviewed as unrelated full subsystems.
No external advisories, web URLs, package downloads, tests, imported code, vulnerability-triggering inputs or PoCs were executed. Candidate recording is left to the parent.
